newsitem.title: GERMANY: German cocoa processors buying at lows - trader.
newsitem.headline: German cocoa processors buying at lows - trader.

text.p: German chocolate manufacturers exploited cocoa futures lows this week, buying beans and semis, trader Albrecht & Dill said in a weekly report on Friday.
Although pausing for the moment, buyers were awaiting further weakness because there was plenty of cocoa around in the short term, it said.
The March position in London earlier this week touched 910 stg but was at 926 at 1535 GMT on Friday, up four.
A&D said new crop arrivals in Ivory Coast ports could not be precisely gauged and available estimates were in a wide range between 90,000 and 180,000 tonnes.
The Ivorian main crop in 1996/97 was estimated unchanged at 900,000-950,000 tonnes.
Current weather patterns were very favourable for mid-crop development.
Main crop qualities were good, with bean sizes at 95 per 100 grammes. Sunny weather aided the drying process and the prevention of mould. --Vera Eckert, Hamburg newsroom, +49-40-41903275
